title: Dynamic Harmonic Rate Limiter and Queued Exit Protocol for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Priya Shah
description: Implement a tenant-aware admission control subsystem for Dedicated fleets that guarantees contracted throughput while holding latency SLOs during bursts. The design combines a dynamic harmonic rate limiter (per-tenant), a multi-tier queuing strategy with demotion lanes, and a queued-exit (ejection) protocol that gracefully sheds overload while preserving high-priority work. The goal is predictable throughput guarantees, transparent failure modes, and operational knobs for autoscaler and fleet controllers.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant steady-state throughput contracts enforced within +/-10% under normal load
P95 tail latency degradation capped to defined SLOs for tiered priorities up to defined burst headroom
Automatic soft-shedding: low-priority queued requests are ejected preferentially under sustained overload
Telemetry shows rate limiter decisions, queue occupancy by lane, and ejection events (sufficient for alerting)
Canary rollout on a single dedicated pool with feature flag and rollback plan
plan: 1) Implement harmonic rate limiter module and integrate with routing proxy. 2) Add multi-lane queueing in the ingress path (fast lane, standard lane, demotion lane). 3) Implement queued-exit protocol with exponential ejection backoff policy. 4) Wire telemetry and dashboards, run perf tests, iterate on thresholds. 5) Canary rollout and measure impact, then broader rollout.
progress_updates: 2026-03-03: Spike completed for harmonic limiter math and simulation harness (microbench shows stable behavior under synthetic bursts).
2026-03-06: Prototype ingress hook implemented; basic queue lanes present in test proxy. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimectl/pull/2174

2026-03-09: First integration test failed under long-tail IO; discovered contention in kv-cache path when large number of queued requests wake concurrently. Added jitter to dequeue and a soft-stagger approach.
2026-03-12: Telemetry schema agreed in runtime-telemetry RFC; dashboards scaffolded in Grafana. Performance test plan drafted (link below).
2026-03-14: Ready for internal canary on pool-dedicated-us-west-2 with config=harmonic-v1. Feature flag 'hazel.admission.dynamic_harmonic' created.
decisions: Use a harmonic rate limiter function (harmonic mean of recent rates and burst allowance) to smooth enforcement and avoid oscillations vs. simple token-bucket
Multi-lane queuing chosen over single FIFO because it allows preserving latency SLOs for priority classes while still allowing bursting
Queued-exit chosen instead of immediate reject: prefer controlled ejection for low-priority work so higher-priority and in-flight work remains unaffected
Ejection policy will be exponential backoff-based with tenant-level cool-down to prevent thundering requeues
tradeoffs_and_risks: Complexity: harmonic limiter requires tuning; initial thresholds may be conservative leading to capacity underuse
KV-cache contention: queued bursts can thundering herding effect when a batch of requests wake and access shared caches (mitigated with staggered dequeue and cache read-rate limiting),
Observability gap: until telemetry is fully wired, diagnosis of false ejections will be harder
Customer experience: customers with many low-priority requests may see increased 429/503s during sustained overload; need transparent docs and per-tenant observability
open_questions: Should the rate limiter be colocated in the ingress proxy or implemented as a standalone admission microservice?
What default per-tenant burst headroom should we expose vs. require explicit SLA/contract?
How should this interact with Dedicated autoscaler decisions when steady overload is detected? (trigger immediate scale vs. continue soft-shedding)
What UX should Console show for ejected requests and recommended mitigation for customers?
testing_plan: Unit tests for harmonic limiter edge cases (zero rate, sudden ramp down)
Load tests with mixed-priority traffic and synthetic KV-cache hot keys to validate staggers
Chaos tests: inject delayed dequeues and simulate downstream stalls to ensure graceful degradation
Canary: 48h canary on single pool with traffic mirror of 5% and active alerting on ejection rate > threshold
rollout_notes: Feature flag gating for all changes. Default OFF for existing customers.
Canary group: pool-dedicated-us-west-2 -> expand to regional pools if stable.
Operator runbook: step-by-step rollback (flip feature flag), kill ingress replicas if needed, raise SRE pager if ejection spike > 1% sustained.
Customer comms: notify customers on Dedicated > invite-only initial canary and provide per-tenant ejection dashboards
